categories.title: CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation)
categories.subtitle: Chest Compressions & Resuscitation
categories.warning: Call 911 / EMS immediately. Send someone for an AED if available.

steps.title: Check Scene Safety & Patient Response
steps.content: Verify the scene is safe for you and the victim. Tap the shoulders firmly and shout loudly: 'Are you okay?'.
steps.explanation: Do not enter toxic, electrical, or traffic hazards. If unresponsive and not breathing or only gasping, immediate CPR is required.
steps.caution: Do not spend more than 10 seconds checking for normal breathing.

steps.title: Call 911 & Request an AED
steps.content: Direct a specific person: 'You, call 911 and find an AED!'. If you are alone with a mobile phone, call 911 and put it on speaker.
steps.explanation: Early defibrillation combined with high-quality chest compressions gives the highest survival probability.
steps.caution: Keep dispatcher on speakerphone while starting compressions.

steps.title: Hand Placement & High-Quality Compressions
steps.content: Place the heel of one hand in the center of the chest (lower half of breastbone). Interlock fingers of second hand. Lock your elbows.
steps.explanation: Push hard and fast: 2 inches (5 cm) deep at a rate of 100 to 120 beats per minute (to the rhythm of 'Stayin' Alive').
steps.caution: Allow complete chest recoil between compressions. Do not lean on chest.

steps.title: Continuous Compressions & Rescue Breaths
steps.content: Perform 30 compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths if trained (tilt head, lift chin, pinch nose). If untrained, perform Hands-Only continuous compressions.
steps.explanation: Hands-Only CPR delivers continuous forward blood flow to the brain and myocardium until paramedics arrive.
steps.caution: Switch compressors every 2 minutes if someone else is available to avoid fatigue.

categories.title: Severe Bleeding
categories.subtitle: Pressure, Hemostasis & Tourniquet
categories.warning: Spurting or pooling blood can cause shock within minutes. Act immediately.

steps.title: Expose Wound & Apply Direct Firm Pressure
steps.content: Tear or cut clothing away from the wound. Place clean gauze, cloth, or your gloved hand directly over the bleeding vessel and push with maximum body weight.
steps.explanation: Direct compression occludes the ruptured lumen and allows platelets to form an initial plug.
steps.illustration_label: Firm Direct Pressure with Clean Dressing
steps.caution: Do not remove pressure to check if bleeding has stopped.

steps.title: Pack Wound if Deep
steps.content: If bleeding is in a junction (groin, armpit, neck) or deep muscle cavity, pack gauze deep into the wound cavity until packed tight, then press down firmly.
steps.explanation: Hemostatic gauze or standard sterile gauze creates internal hydrostatic resistance against the bleeding artery.
steps.caution: Do not pack wounds into the chest or abdomen.

steps.title: Apply Pressure Bandage or Tourniquet
steps.content: Wrap tightly with an elastic or roller bandage. For severe extremity arterial spurting, apply a commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches above the wound (not over a joint).
steps.explanation: Tighten the windlass until bleeding stops completely. Note the exact time of tourniquet application.
steps.caution: Never loosen or release a tourniquet once applied.

categories.title: Burns
categories.subtitle: Thermal, Chemical & Scald Treatment
categories.warning: Never apply ice, butter, oil, or toothpaste to burns.

steps.title: Stop the Burning Source
steps.content: Safely remove the patient from heat, steam, chemical contact, or electrical power. Extinguish burning clothes (Stop, Drop, and Roll).
steps.explanation: Arresting heat transfer limits the progression of dermal and subcutaneous necrosis.
steps.caution: Ensure your own safety before approaching chemical or electrical hazards.

steps.title: Cool with Running Tap Water for 20 Minutes
steps.content: Hold the burned tissue under cool (15-20°C / 59-68°F) running tap water for a full 20 minutes.
steps.explanation: Cool running water dissipates heat trapped in dermal collagen and reduces depth of burn injury.
steps.caution: Do NOT use ice or freezing water, which induces severe vasoconstriction and hypothermia.

steps.title: Remove Jewelry & Constrictive Items
steps.content: Carefully remove rings, watches, bracelets, and tight clothing near the burned area before inflammatory swelling begins.
steps.explanation: Post-burn edema develops rapidly and constrictive items can compromise distal blood supply.
steps.caution: Do not pull fabric that has melted and adhered directly to raw flesh.

steps.title: Cover with Clean, Non-Stick Sterile Dressing
steps.content: Loosely apply clear plastic cling film or a sterile, non-adherent dressing over the burn area. Keep the patient warm.
steps.explanation: Plastic wrap shields exposed nerve endings from air currents (reducing pain) and prevents bacterial contamination.
steps.caution: Do not wrap cling wrap tightly around circumferences of limbs.

steps.title: Clinical Evaluation & Triage
steps.content: Seek immediate hospital care if the burn is larger than the palm of a hand, on face, hands, joints, genitals, or caused by chemicals/electricity.
steps.explanation: Major burns require fluid resuscitation, professional debridement, and tetanus immunization.
steps.caution: Never burst blisters; blister roofs protect against infection.

categories.title: Choking Relief
categories.subtitle: Airway Obstruction & Heimlich Maneuver
categories.warning: If the victim becomes unconscious, support them to the ground and start CPR.

steps.title: Assess Obstruction & Encourage Coughing
steps.content: Ask: 'Are you choking?'. If the person can speak, cough forcefully, or breathe, encourage them to continue coughing hard.
steps.explanation: Spontaneous coughing is the most effective physiological mechanism to clear foreign body airway obstructions.
steps.caution: Do not interfere with coughing if they can still move air.

steps.title: Deliver 5 Sharp Back Blows
steps.content: Stand to the side and slightly behind. Support the victim's chest with one hand and lean them forward. Deliver 5 sharp blows between shoulder blades with heel of hand.
steps.explanation: Forward leaning directs dislodged debris out through the mouth rather than back down into the trachea.
steps.caution: Ensure the victim is leaned forward before delivering blows.

steps.title: Deliver 5 Abdominal Thrusts (Heimlich)
steps.content: Stand behind. Place a fist thumb-side in just above the navel. Grasp fist with other hand and pull sharply inward and upward 5 times.
steps.explanation: Upward diaphragm compression forces residual lung volume upward, generating an artificial cough to expel the object.
steps.caution: For pregnant or obese individuals, deliver chest thrusts over center of breastbone.

categories.title: Bone Injuries & Fractures
categories.subtitle: Splinting, Immobilization & Alignment
categories.warning: Never attempt to straighten a deformed bone or push protruding bone back inside.

steps.title: Immobilize the Injured Limb
steps.content: Instruct the patient to remain completely still. Support the limb manually above and below the suspected fracture site.
steps.explanation: Preventing bone movement stops sharp fragments from severing adjacent arteries, veins, and peripheral nerves.
steps.caution: Do not test range of motion or force weight-bearing.

steps.title: Apply a Rigid or Soft Splint
steps.content: Apply a rolled magazine, cardboard, or padded splint along the limb. Secure with bandages or cloth ties without compressing circulation.
steps.explanation: Splinting must immobilize the joint above and the joint below the fracture location.
steps.caution: Verify finger/toe warmth and pulse before and after splinting.

steps.title: Cold Pack & Elevate
steps.content: Apply a cold pack wrapped in a cloth for 15-20 minutes to reduce edema and pain. Elevate limb above heart level only if splinted securely.
steps.explanation: Cryotherapy limits cellular metabolic rate and inflammatory swelling.
steps.caution: Never place direct ice on bare skin.

categories.title: Unconsciousness
categories.subtitle: Airway Protection & Recovery Position
categories.warning: If normal breathing is absent or gasping, begin CPR immediately.

steps.title: Assess Airway & Breathing
steps.content: Gently tilt the head back and lift the chin. Look, listen, and feel for normal rhythmic breathing for up to 10 seconds.
steps.explanation: In an unconscious patient lying supine, the tongue relaxes and falls against the posterior pharyngeal wall, blocking the trachea.
steps.caution: Do not tilt head if cervical spine injury is suspected; use jaw thrust.

steps.title: Place into Lateral Recovery Position
steps.content: Extend nearest arm out. Bring far arm across chest. Bend far leg up at knee. Gently roll patient toward you onto their side.
steps.explanation: Lateral positioning allows saliva and emesis to drain freely by gravity, preventing fatal aspiration pneumonia.
steps.caution: Ensure the mouth stays lowest and airway remains tilted open.

steps.title: Continuous Vital Sign Monitoring
steps.content: Stay beside the patient. Constantly verify breathing until emergency medical services take over. Keep them warm with a blanket.
steps.explanation: Unconscious patients can deteriorate rapidly into respiratory or cardiac arrest.
steps.caution: Be prepared to flip patient to back and start CPR if breathing ceases.

categories.title: Wound Care & Dressings
categories.subtitle: Irrigation, Antiseptic & Bandaging
categories.warning: Seek medical care if wound is deep, gaping, from an animal, or caused by rusty metal.

steps.title: Clean Hands & Irrigate Wound
steps.content: Wash hands. Rinse the wound under gentle running potable water or saline for 5 minutes to flush out dirt and contaminants.
steps.explanation: Copious gentle irrigation reduces bacterial burden by mechanical washout without causing cellular toxicity.
steps.caution: Do not scrub open wound tissue or use harsh undiluted alcohol.

steps.title: Disinfect & Apply Antibiotic Barrier
steps.content: Pat edges dry with clean sterile gauze. Apply an antiseptic or thin layer of petroleum jelly/antibiotic ointment.
steps.explanation: Maintaining a moist, sterile wound bed accelerates epithelial migration and reduces scarring.
steps.caution: Avoid harsh hydrogen peroxide which can inhibit granulation.

steps.title: Secure with Sterile Dressing
steps.content: Cover completely with a sterile bandage or adhesive dressing. Change dressing daily or immediately if it becomes wet or dirty.
steps.explanation: Sterile occlusion protects against external environmental pathogens.
steps.caution: Watch for signs of infection: increasing redness, heat, swelling, or pus.

categories.title: Poisonings & Toxins
categories.subtitle: Ingestion, Inhalation & Chemical Contact
categories.warning: Do NOT induce vomiting unless specifically directed by Poison Control.

steps.title: Identify Substance & Call Poison Control
steps.content: Determine what was ingested/inhaled, when, and estimated amount. Immediately contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222 in US) or 911.
steps.explanation: Poison management depends entirely on chemical class (acid, alkali, hydrocarbon, prescription drug).
steps.caution: Do not administer raw milk, activated charcoal, or salt water without orders.

steps.title: Decontaminate Exposure Route
steps.content: If inhaled, move to fresh air. If on skin or in eyes, flush with clean water for at least 15 minutes. If conscious and told to, sip water.
steps.explanation: Diluting external chemicals reduces caustic burn severity to skin and corneas.
steps.caution: Never induce vomiting after swallowing bleach, gasoline, or strong acids.

steps.title: Monitor Airway & Retain Container
steps.content: Place unconscious breathing victim in recovery position. Keep the exact chemical container, pill bottle, or plant sample for paramedics.
steps.explanation: Physical product packaging confirms exact CAS numbers and formulation concentrations for antidotes.
steps.caution: Ensure responders are aware of hazardous fumes or skin contamination.

categories.title: Allergies & Anaphylaxis
categories.subtitle: EpiPen Autoinjector & Airway Management
categories.warning: Difficulty breathing, throat tightness, or facial swelling requires immediate epinephrine.

steps.title: Recognize Anaphylaxis Signs & Call 911
steps.content: Check for hives, lip/tongue swelling, stridor, wheezing, dizziness, or vomiting. Call emergency services immediately.
steps.explanation: Anaphylaxis causes systemic vasodilation and bronchial constriction which can occlude airway in minutes.
steps.caution: Do not delay epinephrine to wait for antihistamines like Benadryl.

steps.title: Administer Epinephrine Autoinjector (EpiPen)
steps.content: Grip autoinjector. Pull off safety cap. Push orange tip firmly into outer mid-thigh at 90-degree angle until it clicks. Hold firmly for 3 full seconds.
steps.explanation: Intramuscular epinephrine rapidly reverses bronchospasm, stabilizes mast cells, and raises arterial blood pressure.
steps.caution: Can be administered directly through clothing if necessary.

steps.title: Position Patient & Prepare Second Dose
steps.content: Have patient lie flat with legs elevated. If breathing is difficult, allow them to sit up slightly. If no improvement after 5 minutes, give a second autoinjector.
steps.explanation: Lying flat prevents empty-ventricle syndrome and cardiac collapse from pooling blood.
steps.caution: Do NOT allow the patient to suddenly stand up or walk.

categories.title: Bites & Stings
categories.subtitle: Insect Stings, Venom & Animal Bites
categories.warning: If breathing difficulty develops after a sting, treat immediately for anaphylaxis.

steps.title: Remove Stinger & Wash Area
steps.content: Scrape bee stingers off with a flat fingernail or credit card edge. Wash animal bites or stings thoroughly with soap and water for 5 minutes.
steps.explanation: Scraping avoids squeezing the venom sac attached to the stinger barbs.
steps.caution: Do not squeeze the stinger with tweezers, which injects remaining venom.

steps.title: Apply Cold Compress
steps.content: Wrap an ice pack in a clean towel and apply for 10-15 minutes to reduce localized histamine edema and pain.
steps.explanation: Localized cooling reduces enzymatic dissemination of venom.
steps.caution: For venomous snakebites, do NOT use ice, tourniquets, or suction.

steps.title: Immobilize & Seek Medical Evaluation
steps.content: For animal/human bites or venomous bites, keep patient calm and quiet. Seek clinical evaluation for antibiotics and tetanus/rabies prophylaxis.
steps.explanation: Animal saliva contains dense polymicrobial flora (e.g. Pasteurella) causing rapid soft tissue infection.
steps.caution: Report wild or unknown animal bites immediately to public health.
